Series::abs2¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

Series::abs2() const -> Series
Series& Series::abs2_()

What It Does¶

abs2() returns the squared magnitude of each value: |x|^2.

  • for a real value that is just x * x, identical to square()

  • for a complex value z = a + b i it is a^2 + b^2 — a real, non-negative result, without the intermediate square root that abs() would take

The point of the method is that squared magnitude is what you usually want — energy, power, a squared distance, the denominator of a normalization — and computing it as abs(x) then squaring both does redundant work and, for complex input, throws away the fact that the answer is real.

Parameters¶

None.

Returns¶

Series or Series& |x|^2, elementwise. Real for real input; real and non-negative for complex input. abs2_() overwrites the current storage.

Gradient¶

abs2() is differentiable. For real input it is the square() rule:

d/dx abs2(x) = 2 * x

Examples¶

Example 1. On real input abs2() matches square().

pluss::series::print(std::cout, pluss::make_series({-2.0, 3.0}).abs2());

Output¶

Series(shape=[2], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=2, contiguous=true)
data=[4.0000, 9.0000]

Example 2. The backward multiplier is 2 * x.

auto x = pluss::make_series({-2.0, 3.0, -4.0});
x.tracks_slope_(true);

x.abs2().sum().reverse();

std::cout << "dx=" << x.sensitivity();

Output¶

dx=pluss::Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[-4, 6, -8]

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • For real input, abs2() and square() produce the same values; pick whichever reads better in context.

  • Like square(), the result can overflow for large inputs, and an integer input keeps its dtype.

  • NaN propagates.

Summary¶

abs2(x) is the squared magnitude |x|^2:

  • x * x for real input; re^2 + im^2 for complex, giving a real result

  • differentiable, backward multiplier 2 * x on real input

See Also¶

  • Series::square: identical for real input.

  • Series::abs: the magnitude itself, sqrt(abs2(x)).

  • Series::hypot: sqrt(a^2 + b^2) from two separate real series.
